newsitem.title: FRANCE: French troops said in Zaire, France denies report.
newsitem.headline: French troops said in Zaire, France denies report.

text.p: A Paris newspaper said on Friday that French army intelligence-gathering commandos had been sent into the field in Zaire where rebel forces are threatening President Mobutu Sese Seko's government.
Defence Ministry spokesman Pierre Servent said he "firmly and categorically" denied the report in the Roman Catholic daily La Croix.
The only French army personnel in Zaire were a handful of paramilitary gendarmes guarding France's embassy in Kinshasa as well as the military attache in that mission, Servent said.

La Croix identified the troops it said were in Zaire as members of the army's 13th Parachute Dragoons Regiment, which operated behind Iraqi lines in the Gulf War, and teams from the Parachute Commando Group, a unit involved in all France's African military ventures.
"For the time being, their missions are solely to gather intelligence," said La Croix. Both units are trained to secretly gather information behind enemy lines.
The Tutsi-led rebels, backed by several East African countries, have seized a swathe of east Zaire and frustrated Zaire's much-trumpeted army counter-offensive by opening up new fronts.
The rebels have accused Paris of recruiting and paying foreign mercenaries, including Frenchmen, hired by the Zaire army to help in the counter-offensive.
France, which backs Mobutu but says it obeys international embargoes barring military aid to the region, has denied having anything to do with the mercenaries.
Zaire says Rwanda and Uganda have sent their own troops into Zaire to back the rebels.
The United States has called for neighbouring countries to stay out of the civil war.
